events.text: An old man sits on the hill every time someone in the province faces a heavenly tribulation. He has watched three hundred. He came to watch yours, and he is taking notes.

effects.log: 'How they stand,' he says. 'Most lean forward. The ones who live lean back.'
He does not mind. He writes it down.

events.text: The tribulation watcher is dying, and wants to give his notes to someone who has stood under the bolts and lived. Three hundred tribulations, every one described.

effects.log: Three hundred ways to stand under the sky. You understand, finally, why the ones who live lean back.
The next generation's tribulations go a little better because of him. You put his name on the cover.

events.text: The tree you sheltered under during your last tribulation is dead, black, and humming. A carpenter of the old school says lightning-struck wood from a tribulation is worth a sect's treasury.

effects.log: A black wooden sword that cuts like steel and crackles in the rain.
He nearly cries with joy. You buy a house with a better tree.

events.text: A farmer comes to your gate: your last tribulation's lightning burned his barn and his ox. He is not angry. He would like to know who to send the bill to.

effects.log: He goes home happy. Heaven, they say, notices that kind of thing.

choices.text: Tell him to send it to heaven

effects.log: He actually does: a letter burned at the temple. The next storm misses his farm and hits yours.

events.text: The farmer's son, now grown, faces his own first tribulation. Your old debt makes him family, in a way. He asks you to stand on the hill.

choices.text: Stand beside him under the bolts

ok.log: Heaven's bolts split between two people. He lives. You take half of a stranger's storm and stand up after.

fail.log: The bolts do not split. You take the weight of both of you and wake under the hill with the farmer's son kneeling over you, alive, and weeping.

effects.log: Lean back. He does, and lives, and names his first son after you.

events.text: {npc}, your rival of many years, faces a tribulation on the same night as yours. Heaven, in a hurry, sends one storm for both of you. You are on two peaks a li apart.

ok.log: Two storms' worth of lightning. You stand up afterwards, and look across, and {npc} is standing too, staring.

fail.log: Too much sky for one body. You wake in a crater with every bone complaining, and across the valley your rival stands, singed and furious, alive.

effects.log: You both live. Afterwards neither of you mentions it, and both of you remember.
